result.title: PRIME: Frequency-Aware Unified Pruning and Merging for MoE Compression
result.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have emerged as an effective paradigm for scaling large language models, yet their massive parameter footprint poses severe memory challenges for deployment. Existing compression methods typically treat expert pruning and merging as disjoint operations and rely on greedy heuristics, often leading to irreversible information loss or representational pollution. In this paper, we propose PRIME, a unified optimization framework for MoE compression via adaptive PRunIng and MErging. PRIME casts the discrete prune-merge assignment step as a global Integer Linear Programming over a frequency-weighted surrogate objective, jointly selecting pruning and merging decisions while accounting for expert usage. We motivate the frequency-aware objective through an error-bound analysis under fixed representative assignments, and show that the formulation favors high-frequency experts as centroids, promoting routing stability. Extensive experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B demonstrate that PRIME achieves strong accuracy retention across knowledge, coding, math, and long-context tasks, while serving benchmarks of merged models quantify the memory and throughput benefits of expert compression in vLLM.

AI.brief_summary: PRIME 提出 MoE 模型压缩的统一框架，把专家剪枝与合并的离散分配统一建模为使用频率加权的整数线性规划，并在 Qwen3-30B-A3B 与 Qwen3.5-122B-A10B 上验证精度保留与部署端的显存、吞吐收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作处理的是纯文本 MoE 的冗余单元剪枝与合并，与 LVR 主线无直接联系，但其「按使用频率选代表、统一分配可合并单元」的表述可能为 latent 状态或视觉 token 的冗余合并与表示压缩提供借鉴线索，需核查是否可迁移。
